subject: botany
question_text: What do the terms algal bloom and red tides signify?

verification.note: Sourced from the Junior Fastrack botany book, Biological Classification chapter (book pp.4-5), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star ranks and NO year citations. Only ONE source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this card, not merely pending: 'not checked' must never be read as 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book prints 'Medeterranian' (spelling) and says the algal bloom causes eutrophication; standard botany runs the other way — nutrient-rich (eutrophic) water allows the bloom, and the bloom then harms the water body — and the card states the standard relation, recording the book's position in the step's why.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Algal bloom
lines: Excessive growth of cyanobacteria in stagnant,
polluted water is called an algal bloom.
It lowers water quality and kills fish.
steps.why: Cyanobacteria multiply fast in nutrient-rich, stagnant water; the thick growth colours the water and uses up oxygen as it decays, so fish die. (The book prints that the bloom causes eutrophication; in standard botany, eutrophication — nutrient enrichment — is what allows the bloom, and the bloom then damages the water body.)
common_mistakes: Placing algal blooms in the sea. The bloom described here is in stagnant, polluted water bodies.
Leaving out the harm. The effect on water quality and fish is part of what the term signifies.
steps.memory_tip: Bloom = too much cyanobacterial growth in still, polluted water.
steps.margin_note: Definition plus one effect line earns this mark.

steps.label: Red tides
lines: rapidly that the sea appears red, as in the
red tides of the Mediterranean Sea.
Their toxins kill fish and other marine animals.
steps.why: The red colour is only the visible sign; the danger of a red tide is the toxins the multiplying Gonyaulax cells release into the sea.
common_mistakes: Naming Nostoc or Anabaena here. Red tides are caused by the dinoflagellate Gonyaulax.
Writing only the colour change and not the toxin effect.
steps.memory_tip: Red tide: red dinoflagellate, red sea — Gonyaulax is the name to write.
steps.margin_note: The name Gonyaulax and the toxin effect are the two things to write.

insider_note: The two terms are marked separately, and the organism names — cyanobacteria and Gonyaulax — are what the examiner underlines.
